A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoV, despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, retrieval and prompt-pool ablations, transfer experiments, and timing measurements in Section 4 and Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 reports revised evaluations and ablations, additional benchmark results in Table 5, and original repeated-seed results in Table 6.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 adds an inference pre-filter that removes the candidate whose visual features are farthest from the others by cosine distance. The feature extraction, ranking architecture, pairwise reward loss, and highest-ranked-prompt decoding remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from six to fifteen benchmarks. Table 1 adds MMStar and MathVista; new Table 5 adds CVBench, BLINK, Real-World QA, MMVP, COCO2017 captioning, RefCOCO+ grounding, and ImageNet-1K classification, substantially extending task coverage. The training-data sources remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the base models, FGVP, Circle, API, fixed-prompt retrieval, random retrieval, and MoE/GateNet. New Table 5 uses existing base-model and API comparators. VTPrompt and TVP enter the candidate-pool ablation, rather than being evaluated as standalone competing methods.

E3.justification: The main candidate pool changes from four API attention prompts to those four plus RedCircle and FGVP. Table 3 also changes the cumulative prompt sequence and tests sizes 1–8 instead of 2–8. Backbone sizes and the reported training budget, batch size, and learning rate remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing pool-size sensitivity study is revised to introduce a one-prompt condition and VTPrompt/TVP candidates, replacing the earlier expansion through additional attention layers. Retrieval comparisons, transfer analyses, and qualitative cases are retained. The new inference filter is not separately ablated.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, v2 includes a statistical-significance section and appendix reporting five MMMU seeds, paired t-testing, a mean difference, standard deviation, and a p-value threshold. This newly documents repeated-run evidence; it does not establish an increase over v1's undisclosed run count. The reported mean gain of 2.06 points conflicts with Table 6's differences, which average 2.46.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 extensively revise AutoV and comparator scores, and Tables 5–6 add benchmark and repeated-run results. For example, LLaVA-OneVision's VizWiz scores change from 59.4 to 68.4 for AutoV and 58.7 to 66.9 for API. AutoV's changed pool and inference procedure prevent treating its revision as a same-setting gain. Table 4's closed-source results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same feature extraction, interaction, scoring, reward-loss, and attention-prompt mathematics. Assignment notation and explanatory wording change, but neither version adds formal theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains automated, query-conditioned visual-prompt ranking. v2 adds an explicit introductory claim of generalization to captioning, grounding, and classification, and strengthens quantitative headline claims, including Qwen2.5-VL's MMMU improvement from 1.9 to 3.8 points.

C2.justification: v1's limitations discussion concerning teacher strength, frozen-parameter reuse, and prompt quality is removed. The pool-size interpretation changes from acknowledging small degradations to asserting that individually harmful prompts preserve or improve performance. The recommended pool limit also changes from fewer than five to fewer than seven candidates.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies LLaVA-OneVision as the retrieval source for the closed-source models, specifies the API layer/color variants used in qualitative examples, and quantifies additional inference computation as 0.8 TFLOPs. Existing training-data composition, hardware, optimizer framework, epochs, batch size, and learning rate are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds an explicit distinction from RORA-VLM and Re-Align, contrasting internal prompt selection with external retrieval and model fine-tuning. References also expand for added prompt types, benchmarks, and statistical methods. The overall positioning remains adaptive visual-prompt retrieval.

P1.justification: The title changes to Loss-Oriented Ranking for Automated Visual Prompting in LVLMs, several analysis passages and headings are streamlined, and the supplementary material gains a contents list and reorganized training-data subsections. The main section sequence and much of the methodological prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The document switches from a single-column design to a two-column conference layout. Table 1 gains benchmark columns and revised color coding, Table 3 is transposed and redesigned, and Tables 5–6 are added. Existing diagrams and qualitative figures are largely retained but resized and repositioned; Figure 6's panels change from horizontal to vertical arrangement.

improvement.justification: Broader task coverage and explicit repeated-run evidence strengthen validation, but v2 removes substantive limitations and introduces unresolved numerical inconsistencies. Besides Table 6's incorrect mean summary, Table 1 lists InternVL2 MathVista scores of 58.3 and 70.5 while labeling the difference as 2.2. The added tasks' exact evaluation metrics are also insufficiently specified. These benefits and reliability concerns prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
